name: GitLab CI script line continuations
comment: source.shell starts a command name with a \G rule, which in a .sh file never matches at the start of a line. Inside a script region the YAML grammar's and our own while rules leave \G at the start of every line, so a backslash-continued line would be read as a new command name. Still being inside a command at the start of a line means the line is a continuation, so these rules, which win over \G, read it as more options and arguments instead. They mirror source.shell#option and #argument, anchored to the start of the line so they never compete with an argument's own end.

patterns.comment: A continuation starting with an operator such as || or &&: consume the indent so the command ends at the operator.
